newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians arrest senior police officer.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians arrest senior police officer.

text.p: Palestinian security officials have arrested a senior police officer accused by Israelis of ordering an attack on a rabbi in the West Bank, officials said on Monday.
Deputy Commander Jihad Masouni, who heads a criminal detective unit in Nablus police, is being held in the West Bank town's jail, governor Mahmoud al-Aloul told Reuters.
Two other officers were also under arrest, he said.
Israel has accused Palestinian police of carrying out a shooting attack that damaged the car of a rabbi in the West Bank this month and of planning other attacks on settlers.
Israel demanded that Palestinian police arrest Masouni, charging he plotted the attack.
But Aloul said he doubted the existance of a ring in the Palestinian police dedicated to attacking settlers and wrecking the peace process.
"I don't think so. I think that the Israeli authorities are exaggerating their claim and this story," he said.
"They are trying to move the focus from their violations of the mutual agreements between them and us into small things like this."
Israel arrested three Palestinian police officers last week, saying they were on their way to attack Jews at Har Bracha, a settlement near Palestinian-ruled Nablus in the West Bank.
They arrested another police officer later on suspicion of planning attacks near the West Bank town of Tulkarm.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has called for an immediate change in Palestinian policy. He told reporters on Sunday the authority must "turn police against terror and not towards terror".
Palestinian officials have demanded that Israel hand over the four Palestinians.
"This is an illegal act from the Israeli side because they have to surrender the officers to the Palestinian police, and we have to investigate their involvement in anything illegal," Aloul said.
"We need to complete the investigation, because if we do not investigate these policemen we cannot have a 100 percent evaluation of the situation," he added.
